scan_notes:
Reviewed the exact abbb8e4f...3bcddf31 diff, migration ordering, PostgreSQL adapter/autocommit behavior, role provisioning, all named readers, every remaining `_REAL_PRODUCTS` occurrence, and new file/symbol/test citations.

Boot behavior is correct when boots are sequential: fresh and empty prod databases create only the marker; dev updates exactly the three named rows; later boots skip; a boot begun after an operator promotion preserves it. The single DO statement is transaction-atomic under autocommit, so COMMENT failure rolls back UPDATE. `torque_app` owns application objects via `scripts/sql/create_torque_app.sql`; the preceding every-boot ALTERs already require that ownership. Quoting and `clients` regclass resolution are valid in the supported search path.

Reader propagation is correct: picker entries remain listed but false-badged; `real_product_codes()` and the workbook exclude them; review queue returns non-real/UNKNOWN; page resolution deliberately continues serving non-demo canaries without counting them as real.

All remaining `_REAL_PRODUCTS` references are historical, supersession notes, frozen records, or test-history explanations; I found no remaining actionable instruction relying on the deleted symbol. New paths and test symbols resolve, but two new operational descriptions are false as reported below.

Verification: fact-check range audit passed; citation-resolution tests passed (26); selected affected structure/unit tests passed (100, 11 skipped). The four PostgreSQL backfill tests could not be independently rerun because this sandbox denies localhost TCP connections; this is an environment failure, not a test verdict.

findings.title: Concurrent first boots can overwrite an operator promotion
findings.evidence: `IF NOT EXISTS (...) THEN UPDATE clients SET is_real = 0 ...; COMMENT ON COLUMN ...; END IF;` checks for the absent marker without serializing competing first executions.
findings.failure_scenario: Two new containers start concurrently on the first rollout and both observe no comment. The first commits the backfill and marker; an operator then runs the supported promotion; the second already-admitted DO block resumes and writes the promoted row back to 0 before committing. Thus the marker prevents later sequential boots but not an overlapping first boot.
findings.suggested_fix: Acquire a transaction-scoped advisory lock at the start of the DO block, before checking pg_description, then recheck the marker while holding it. This serializes only this migration and does not lock the served clients table on no-op boots.

findings.title: One-shot test allows a weaker data-state guard to pass
findings.evidence: The test promotes only `silver_canary`, then explicitly leaves `browser_drill_co` and `tor682_canary` at 0: `assert after["browser_drill_co"] == 0 and after["tor682_canary"] == 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: A weaker migration guarded by “skip whenever any named canary is already 0” passes every test: after the first run two untouched rows remain 0, so the tested single promotion survives. If an operator promotes all three canaries, however, the next boot sees no zero sentinel and demotes all three again.
findings.suggested_fix: Promote all three rows before the repeated boots and assert all remain 1. Also assert that the column comment exists after the first migration, independently of row values.

findings.title: Atomic UPDATE/marker requirement is not tested
findings.evidence: Every test exercises successful `init_db()` calls and resulting rows; none checks that UPDATE and COMMENT remain in one migration statement or forces a failure after UPDATE.
findings.failure_scenario: A future refactor splits the guarded UPDATE and COMMENT into successive `_PG_MIGRATIONS` entries. All current tests remain green. If COMMENT is then cancelled by a lock timeout on first boot, autocommit has already committed the UPDATE without its marker, rearming the migration.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a structural assertion that the named UPDATE and COMMENT occur in the same single DO migration entry, or an integration control that proves a post-UPDATE exception rolls back both effects.

findings.title: `tenant create` is not a valid torque-admin command
findings.evidence: The new instruction says ``torque-admin tenant create` writes it into the `clients` registry`, but `scripts/torque_admin.py` defines tenant subcommands `add`, `list`, and `update`; there is no `tenant create`.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent follows this active prompt while registering a red-team client. argparse rejects `create` as an invalid tenant subcommand, so the client is never registered and the picker step cannot complete.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `tenant create` with the actual `torque-admin tenant add` invocation and show the required `--name`, `--key`, and relevant product/simulation flags.

findings.title: Workbook source map omits product-specific slots
findings.evidence: The new map says `Product/Slot   clients (is_real) x companies._SLOTS`, while `build()` calls `served_slots(code)`, which returns `_SLOTS` plus matching `_PRODUCT_SLOTS`.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader follows the new source map to reproduce or audit the workbook population. For a product such as ALM with product-specific Deal Ops slots, the documented cross-product omits rows that the workbook actually emits.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the source as real routable `client_registry.tenants()` crossed with `served_slots(code)`, explicitly including matching `_PRODUCT_SLOTS`.

findings.title: Migration comment cites the wrong writer and CLI syntax
findings.evidence: The comment names ``torque-admin tenant update <slug> --real`` and then states ``api/services/vault/clients.py` is the only production writer of this column.` The parser requires `tenant update --slug <slug> --real`, and `api/services/control_plane/tenants.py` performs the production UPDATE of `is_real`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator copies the documented command and argparse rejects the positional slug. Separately, a maintainer auditing the claimed sole writer inspects the vault INSERT path but misses the supported update path that owns later operator decisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `torque-admin tenant update --slug <slug> --real` and cite `api/services/vault/clients.py` for insertion plus `api/services/control_plane/tenants.py` for updates.

overall_explanation: The migration’s sequential boot semantics, transaction atomicity, permissions, reader propagation, and explicit slug selection are sound. The material defect is an unhandled concurrent-first-boot race. The tests also admit weaker one-shot and non-atomic implementations, and the citation sweep introduced several false operational descriptions.
